executive_policy.note: Party leadership and national office are separate roles. Calendar references and party chairs never schedule a presidency.

Radical 1993/1994 succession conflict and exact date unresolved.

PPDF's July 1995 formation still needs a primary statutory record. The November 25 Force démocrate transition is supported; the exact end of Santini's PSD executive role and the other merger participants' office transitions remain unresolved.

UDF split/transition into MoDem, Nouveau Centre and other currents; legal residual UDF and later revival/name-use questions unresolved. Separate game identities and branch-specific leadership research required.

parties.identity_note: 1990 UDF was a federation of distinct political organizations. Its federal president is recorded alongside constituent executives, not as their replacement. The 1998 Nouvelle UDF reorganization merged some components while others remained associated or departed. MoDem, Nouveau Centre, UMP and later organizations are separate branches; this row is not assigned an invented single 2007–2026 successor chain.

institution.fact: Constitution articles 6 and 7 separate the directly elected President of the Republic from party leadership; article 8 gives the President appointment of the Prime Minister.
institution.gameplay_assumption: A party first secretary, party president or constituent leader is not automatically a national president. future_leadership_seats.gameplay_assumption: Choose the paired option for an empty future leadership and preserve documented paired leadership after vacancies. A surviving historical single chair is not converted automatically. Entirely fictional pairs use an authored woman/man team as a conservative game policy; this does not assert a universal legal prohibition of other teams. An unclassified historical co-holder remains unchanged and a fictional woman is selected beside that person without claiming the mixed team's full quota eligibility has been researched. The game does not simulate congress choice, nominations or all statutory qualifications.
future_leadership_seats.institutional_fact: The published federal organizational statute, section 23, permits a single chair or two equal chairs including a woman, as decided by the party congress. The 2025 proposal explicitly enabling a two-woman federal pair was referred rather than adopted in the published resolutions.
future_leadership_seats.qualification_note: Historical incumbent qualifications are not inferred; mixed-team quota eligibility is not claimed as fully researched.

future_leadership_seats.gameplay_assumption: Retain the two-chair structure through 2035 and fill only vacancies reached through existing campaign succession events. Fictional seat qualifications are explicitly authored, not inferred from names or art. Preserve all historical incumbents, including a surviving three-person board. Historical gender qualifications are unreviewed here: an unknown surviving co-holder is never relabeled, and a newly added fictional woman supplies the minimum confirmed representation. The game does not implement the full board, nomination votes, mandate restrictions or electoral procedure.
future_leadership_seats.institutional_fact: The federal statute updated 1 July 2026, section 17(2), provides for two equal chairs, at least one a woman. Section 17(5) distinguishes a replacement election from the ordinary board election.
future_leadership_seats.qualification_note: Historical incumbent qualifications are not inferred; mixed-team quota eligibility is not claimed as fully researched.

future_leadership_seats.gameplay_assumption: Choose the paired option for an empty future leadership and preserve documented paired leadership after vacancies. A surviving historical single chair is not converted automatically. Entirely fictional pairs use an authored woman/man team as a conservative game policy; this does not assert a universal legal prohibition of other teams. An unclassified historical co-holder remains unchanged and a fictional woman is selected beside that person without claiming the mixed team's full quota eligibility has been researched. The game does not simulate congress choice, nominations or all statutory qualifications.
future_leadership_seats.institutional_fact: The published federal organizational statute, section 23, permits a single chair or two equal chairs including a woman, as decided by the party congress. The 2025 proposal explicitly enabling a two-woman federal pair was referred rather than adopted in the published resolutions.
future_leadership_seats.qualification_note: Historical incumbent qualifications are not inferred; mixed-team quota eligibility is not claimed as fully researched.

Fictional seat qualifications are explicitly authored, not inferred from names or art. Preserve all historical incumbents, including a surviving three-person board. The game does not implement the full board, nomination votes, mandate restrictions or electoral procedure.
future_leadership_seats.institutional_fact: The federal statute updated 1 July 2026, section 17(2), provides for two equal chairs, at least one a woman. Section 17(5) distinguishes a replacement election from the ordinary board election.
